finding.claim: The purge handler calls checkPerm(u, "admin") but discards the boolean result, so any authenticated user can trigger purgeAll().
finding.source: Authenticated request; the caller's *User is taken from request context via userFrom(r) (handlers.go:25, 40). Precondition: the caller's Perms map lacks "admin", and the route is reachable by non-admin users (route registration not in this directory).
finding.sink: purgeAll() at handlers.go:27, a destructive operation over all data.

trace.note: u := userFrom(r) loads the caller from request context.
checkPerm(u, "admin") returns a bool that is never read.
checkPerm returns u.Perms[perm] with no enforcement side effect.
mustPerm, the enforcing helper that writes 403 and returns false, is not called in purge.
rotateKeys uses mustPerm correctly, showing the admin check was intended for this handler.

finding.guards_checked: checkPerm (return value ignored, so no enforcement); mustPerm (correct helper, not invoked by purge); no middleware or router-level guard visible in this directory; route registration for purge not present, so a router-level admin restriction cannot be ruled out. userFrom type assertion panics on missing user but net/http recovers per request, so no bypass from that.

verdict.guard_found: None effective in handlers.go. checkPerm (handlers.go:12-14) returns a bool, and its result is discarded by the bare call at handlers.go:26. mustPerm (handlers.go:16-22), the enforcing helper, is not called in purge. rotateKeys uses mustPerm correctly (handlers.go:33-35). No router or middleware guard is visible in this directory.
verdict.reason: Every trace line matches the code: checkPerm's bool is discarded at handlers.go:26 and purgeAll() runs unconditionally at handlers.go:27, so the missing check is real. Whether a non-admin can reach purge depends on route registration, which is not in this directory and could carry an admin-only middleware, so reachability cannot be decided from the available code.
